I attended Hereticon in 2022, and I had an experience there that made a truly deep impact on me. Getting to the conclusion was a trek for me, so you’re going to have to listen to the whole story.

===

Finally, I hit on the right question. “What is the underlying nature of knowing truth to you? What’s the gold standard for evidence? Everyone has to take a lot on faith, there’s too much to figure it all out. But ultimately, what form of evidence trumps all others?”
↓
1657613626826702848 [2023-05-14] @eshear 💜 278 🔁 19
Interregnum: I encourage you to actually consider this question. What is it that grounds out truth for you? This isn’t a trick question, go with the obvious and naive answer.
↓
1657613628282138626 [2023-05-14] @eshear 💜 177 🔁 4
Srsly think about your answer (and what other people might answer) before you keep reading. It’s more fun that way and you learn more.
↓
1657613629548826627 [2023-05-14] @eshear 💜 343 🔁 29
So eventually he comes to his answer. When someone presents an idea, he connects with them. He looks in their eyes. He considers their motivations. And if their argument is internally consistent with itself. And if all the signs are green, he trusts them and that’s truth.
↓
1657613630974877696 [2023-05-14] @eshear 💜 486 🔁 23
This just blew me away. It’s a fundamentally social theory of truth. Truth is based on credible arguments presented by trustworthy people. 

That is not what truth is to me, at all.
↓
1657613632296095745 [2023-05-14] @eshear 💜 291 🔁 12
For me, the gold standard of truth is what I can see, hear, taste, smell, feel for myself. What is “true” is what my current conceptual model of the world can infer from that data.
↓
1657613633902481408 [2023-05-14] @eshear 💜 239 🔁 8
(Actually truth is whatever reflects the underlying nature of reality, we are talking here only about our current best guess at truth, but this is an unavoidable distinction for finite beings who cannot know Truth)

title: The tweet that breaks “pick a side” logic
summary:
The most quotable takeaway wasn’t even Malcolm Ocean’s paradox—it was DRMacIver’s blunt rule: “People you can’t say ‘I don’t know’ to are not safe to be around.” The whole discourse is basically a pile-on against sides-forcing: SurenVynn (back in 2016) calls “if you’re an ally you MUST be an active ally” the same Bush-era move that erases the third option, and DRMacIver (2021) says the only sane response to “with me or against me” is “fine, guess I’m against you,” because the demand itself is a red flag. Maradydd sharpens it into game theory: trying to make you defect from a third party is itself defection.

What triggered the modern version was Malcolm Ocean inventing a self-referential trap: “If you’re not against ‘if you’re not with us you’re against us’, you’re against us.” It landed as a meme in 2022 (360+ likes) and then became a reusable citation people kept quote-tweeting whenever they saw purity tests. The peak wasn’t just the joke—it was Malcolm’s 2023 clarification that the final “us” shouldn’t be a smug counter-tribe; it’s inclusive (“it’s everybody”), and the real enemy is “collective usness” getting wrecked by binary demands. Around the same time, eshear’s big Hereticon story gave it a concrete map: “team words-mean-things” vs “team alliances,” where some people treat truth as grounded in observation/models, and others ground it in trusting the right people—aka exactly the kind of epistemology that turns “are you with us?” into a loyalty test.

Then it got more serious (and messier): Danielle Fong framed lefty black/white “splitting” as a psychological pattern and called Malcolm’s line “chef’s kiss”; slimepriestess pushed back that refusing sides-pressure can become a fake “civility norm” that protects the powerful, and Malcolm admitted there’s a hypocrisy-shaped edge to his own framing while still defending the core point. By late 2023 the discourse matured into a technical distinction Malcolm made explicit: the bad version asserts an objective fact (“then it IS THE CASE you’re against us”), while the healthier version is perspectival boundary-setting (“if we can’t tell, we’ll take precautions”). The reason anyone should care is the 2025 punchline: nosilverv jokes that having nuanced views now basically bans you from joining any big coalition—and when people like CoreyJMahler go viral with “Pick your side—there are no others” (paired with shock imagery), you can see how quickly “choose a team” stops being rhetorical and starts being social sorting that breaks real-world coordination.
